symptom: Bloom filter lookups drop rows that exist. The file data/bloom_filter.parquet has 4096 rows, one INT32 column named code, and two row groups of 2048 rows. Calling parquetQuery({ file, filter: { code: { $eq: 30 } } }) returns the 1024 rows where code is 30, as expected. Adding useBloomFilters: true to the same call returns an empty array. The same happens for the values 10, 70, and 90. A filter on a value that is not in the file, such as 50, correctly returns an empty array either way.

parquetScan returns an empty range at a row group boundary. The file data/bloom_filter.parquet has 4096 rows in two row groups of 2048 rows. Calling parquetScan({ file, rowStart: 0, rowEnd: 2048 }) and reading the ranges property should give one range, { rowStart: 0, rowEnd: 2048 }. It gives two: that range and a second one, { rowStart: 2048, rowEnd: 2048 }, which covers no rows. Our reader loops over the ranges and trips on the empty one. Starting a scan on a boundary, with rowStart: 2048 and rowEnd: 4096, gives the single range it should.

Reading a file through an asynchronous source fails when the footer is larger than the first fetch. The file data/datapage_v2.snappy.parquet has 5 rows. I wrap its bytes in an object with byteLength and an async slice(start, end) method that returns a promise, like a file behind a network request. parquetReadObjects({ file }) returns the 5 rows. To reproduce the case of a large footer with a small file, I pass initialFetchSize: 64 to the same call. It then rejects with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')" instead of returning the same 5 rows. Wrapping the bytes in an object whose slice returns the buffer directly, with no promise, gives the 5 rows with the same option.
